name: Block 1: 10K base
coachNotes: This block builds your aerobic base with genuinely easy running (aim under 145 bpm, ceiling 150), adds one controlled quality session a week, and grows the long run from 8 to 10 km. Each session is sent to your Apple Watch with pace or HR alerts so the watch keeps you honest: quality sessions should be controlled, never faster than the target pace. Week 4 eases off, then a 5K time trial resets your paces for Block 2 on the way to sub-55. Do 2 x 10-15 min strength sessions weekly (squats, lunges, glute bridges, calf raises) and stretch after every run to keep the knees happy.

glossary.meaning: An easy heart-rate range where you can talk in full sentences. For you that's roughly 130-145 bpm, with 150 as the ceiling. It builds endurance without tiring you out, so most of your running should be here.
Heart rate creeping up during a steady run even though your pace hasn't changed, caused by heat, fatigue and fluid loss. It's normal. Slow down to keep under your ceiling rather than stopping.
If you can speak full sentences you're running easy; a few words at a time is tempo; single words is hard. When the numbers and the talk test disagree, trust the talk test.
Planned walk breaks taken from the start (e.g. 4 min run / 1 min walk), before you're tired. It keeps heart rate down and is far better than being forced to stop later.

Short, smooth accelerations of about 20 s, building to fast but relaxed running (not a sprint), then easing off and walking or jogging back. They practise good form and leg speed without adding fatigue. A heart-rate spike during them is expected.
The hardest pace you could hold for a whole 5K race, about 30 minutes for you. Hard but sustainable: breathing heavily, but in control.
'Comfortably hard' running: you can say a few words but not chat. It trains the pace you can hold for a long time, which is what makes a 10K feel easier.
Moving stretches before running: leg swings forwards and sideways (10 each leg), walking lunges (10 each leg) and a few high knees. They loosen your hips and legs ready for faster running.

An Apple Watch Workout app feature: tap ⋯ on Outdoor Run, then Create Workout › Custom. Add a warm-up, work and recovery steps with repeats and pace or heart-rate alerts, and the watch cues each step for you.
A solo, all-out run over a set distance to measure your current fitness. It sets the paces for your next block.
Rate of Perceived Exertion: how hard it feels on a 1-10 scale. 3 is easy chatting, 6-7 is comfortably hard, 8 is hard, 10 is an all-out sprint.

runs.title: Easy run + strides
runs.targetEffort: Zone 2, aim under 145 bpm, ceiling 150, conversational
runs.purpose: Builds your aerobic base, the foundation for everything faster. The strides at the end keep your legs quick without adding fatigue.
keyPoints: Keep heart rate under 145 bpm and never above 150

segments.label: Easy run
segments.targetEffort: RPE 3/10, can talk in full sentences
segments.instructions: HR drift in the second half is normal. If HR climbs, slow down and shorten your stride before you walk. If you need to walk, use run/walk (4 min run / 1 min walk) from the start.

segments.label: Strides
segments.instructions: Build up over the first 5 s, hold, then ease off. Tall posture, quick light feet. HR spikes during strides are expected.

recoveryStep.label: Walk back
recoveryStep.instructions: Walk or slow jog back, about 60 s

runs.title: 400 m repeats
runs.purpose: Teaches your body to run at 5K effort and builds speed, while short reps keep it manageable.
keyPoints: Never faster than 5:40 /km, even if it feels easy at first

segments.label: Dynamic warm-up
segments.instructions: Leg swings and walking lunges before you start jogging.

segments.label: 400 m reps
segments.instructions: Hard but sustainable: a pace you could hold for about 30 minutes. The first 30 s always feels easy, so don't speed up.

runs.title: Long run
runs.purpose: Builds endurance and gets your body used to time on your feet, the key ingredient for a 10K.
keyPoints: Slow down rather than stop when HR drifts up

segments.label: Long easy run
segments.instructions: Expect HR drift over the second half. Planned walk breaks (e.g. 1 min every 10 min) are fine.

runs.title: 5K time trial
runs.purpose: Measures your current fitness. Your time sets the paces for Block 2; sub-28:30 means you're on track for a sub-55 10K.
keyPoints: Don't go faster than 5:40 /km in the first km

segments.label: Controlled start
segments.instructions: Resist the urge to go faster in the first km. Settle into an even rhythm.

segments.label: Strong finish
segments.targetPace: as fast as you can hold
segments.instructions: Push from here and empty the tank over the final 500 m. Target: under 28:30 for the full 5 km.
